review_notes: I read the whole file and the Mathlib Perm support API. The commute-then-cycle-factor argument and the commutator-fix argument each appear only once. The one repeated block is the proof that a permutation commuting with a permutation c sends the support of c into itself; it appears in k328dax_exists_zpow and in k328dax_commutator_fix. Mathlib already has `Equiv.Perm.mem_support_iff_of_commute` for this. I have not compiled the proposed rewrites. The `mem_support` rewriting in the exists_zpow rewrite is the part most likely to need small adjustment. The point is repeated proof machinery, so this is a modest finding.

findings.problem: The same proof is written twice. Let q commute with a permutation c. Take the commutation equation at t, expand it with `mul_apply`, rewrite, and use injectivity of q to show that q maps the support of c into itself. It appears as `hcq` in k328dax_exists_zpow (c = σ.cycleOf t, lines ~53–58). It appears again as `hsupp` in k328dax_commutator_fix (c = σ, lines 70–76), with the same `congr_fun hq.eq t; simp only [mul_apply] at h; rw [← h]; exact fun h' => … q.injective h'` steps. Mathlib already has this fact as `Equiv.Perm.mem_support_iff_of_commute`, so neither block needs to be re-proved.
findings.proposed_change: Use the existing lemma `Equiv.Perm.mem_support_iff_of_commute {g c : Perm α} (hgc : Commute g c) (x : α) : g x ∈ c.support ↔ x ∈ c.support`. In k328dax_commutator_fix, replace the body of `hsupp` with `fun q hq t ht => (Equiv.Perm.mem_support_iff_of_commute hq t).2 ht`. In k328dax_exists_zpow, replace the `hcq` block with `Equiv.Perm.mem_support.1 ((Equiv.Perm.mem_support_iff_of_commute hq t).2 (Equiv.Perm.mem_support.2 hct))`, which has type `σ.cycleOf t (q t) ≠ q t`. Here `hq : Commute q (σ.cycleOf t)` is already a hypothesis and `hct : σ.cycleOf t t ≠ t`. Both uses keep their current hypotheses and need no new imports, since the lemma is in Mathlib.GroupTheory.Perm.Support.
findings.benefit: This removes about 12 lines of duplicated manual `mul_apply` and injectivity reasoning. Each use becomes a single call to a named library lemma, so a reader sees at once that the support is preserved by commuting elements. Any later change to how support-stability is proved is no longer needed in two places.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem mem_support_iff_of_commute {g c : Perm α} (hgc : Commute g c) (x : α) :
    g x ∈ c.support ↔ x ∈ c.support
have hsupp : ∀ q : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), Commute q σ → ∀ t ∈ σ.support, q t ∈ σ.support := by
